words.definition: A state of matter that has no fixed shape and spreads out to fill its container.
The star at the center of our solar system that gives Earth light and heat.
Water that has frozen solid.
A chemical substance that can react with metals and turns litmus paper red.
The smallest basic unit of a living thing.
A form of energy that makes things warm.
The amount of matter in an object.
A moving disturbance that carries energy, like light or sound.
A push or pull that can change how an object moves.
One of the two organs in the chest used for breathing.
A hard part of the skeleton that supports and protects the body.
A blood vessel that carries blood back to the heart.
A state of matter that holds its own shape.
Hot melted rock that flows from a volcano.
Hot melted rock found beneath the Earth's surface, before it erupts.
A mixture of two or more metals.
The hard outer layer of the Earth, or of certain objects.
A thin fiber that carries messages between the brain and the body.
A tiny germ that can cause disease and needs a living host to reproduce.
A tiny living fungus used to make bread rise.
The regular beat of the heart, felt through blood moving in the arteries.
The regular rise and fall of the ocean's surface caused by the Moon's pull.
A tiny reproductive cell made by fungi, mosses, and some other organisms.
An organ in the body that produces and releases substances like hormones.
The force that pulls objects toward the center of the Earth.
The ability to do work or cause change, such as heat, light, or motion.
A group of atoms bonded together, the smallest unit of a substance.
The natural home or environment of an animal or plant.
A community of living things interacting with their environment.
The process plants use to turn sunlight, water, and carbon dioxide into food.
An object that can attract certain metals, like iron.
A force that slows down or resists movement between two surfaces touching each other.
An instrument used to see distant objects, like stars and planets, up close.
An instrument used to see very small things that can't be seen with the naked eye.
The smallest basic unit of matter that makes up everything around us.
A large round body in space that orbits a star, like Earth orbits the Sun.
The curved path an object follows as it travels around another object in space.
An object that orbits a planet, either natural like the Moon or made by humans.
The process of a liquid turning into a gas, usually due to heat.
The process of a gas turning into a liquid, often seen as water droplets.
A natural solid substance found in the Earth, like quartz or salt.
The preserved remains or traces of an ancient plant or animal.
A substance that living things need to grow and stay healthy.
A complete path that electricity can flow around.
A substance used to help the body build protection against a disease.
Tiny, single-celled living things, some helpful and some that can cause illness.
A light, colorless gas that is the most common element in the universe.
The gas in the air that people and animals need to breathe to live.
The speed of something in a particular direction.
The force an object has because of its motion, based on its mass and speed.
How much mass is packed into a given amount of space.
A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up itself.
Any living thing, from a tiny bacterium to a giant whale.
A thread-like structure in cells that carries genetic information.
The gradual process by which living things change over many generations.
The passing of traits from parents to their offspring.
A complete change in form, such as a caterpillar turning into a butterfly.
The process by which living things take in oxygen and release carbon dioxide for energy.
A material that allows electricity or heat to pass through it easily.
A material that blocks the flow of electricity or heat.
The maximum height of a wave, related to how loud or strong it is.
The number of times something repeats in a certain amount of time, like sound waves per second.
An event where one object in space blocks the light of another, like the Sun or Moon.
A rocky object, smaller than a planet, that orbits the Sun.
A huge cloud of gas and dust in space, often where stars are born.
Water that falls from clouds, such as rain, snow, or hail.
Small solid particles that settle at the bottom of water or are carried by wind.
A solid substance with a regular, repeating pattern of atoms, often forming geometric shapes.
A protein that speeds up chemical reactions inside living things.
A chemical messenger produced by the body that controls how cells and organs work.
A space completely empty of matter, including air.
Energy that travels in waves or particles, such as light or heat from the Sun.
The branch of physics dealing with heat, energy, and how they transfer.
Relating to the interaction of electric and magnetic fields, as in light or radio waves.
Relating to the smallest possible discrete unit of energy or matter.
A version of an element with a different number of neutrons in its atoms.
The movement of water through a membrane from an area of low to high concentration.
The movement of particles from an area of high concentration to low concentration.
The part of a cell that produces energy, often called the "powerhouse of the cell."
The green pigment in plants that captures light energy for photosynthesis.
The variety of living things found in a particular ecosystem or on Earth.
A close relationship between two different living things, often benefiting both.
The rate at which an object's speed or direction changes over time.
The tendency of an object to resist a change in its motion.
The full range of colors or wavelengths that light can be separated into.
The distance between two identical points on a repeating wave.
The central part of an atom or a cell, holding most of its mass or genetic material.
words.riddle: Every atom and every cell has one of me at its center. What am I?

words.definition: A measure of disorder or randomness in a system.
words.riddle: The messier a room gets over time, the more of me there is. What am I?

words.definition: Relating to heat that comes from deep within the Earth.
An animal that has a backbone, such as a fish, bird, or mammal.
An animal that does not have a backbone, such as an insect or worm.
An organism that lives on or in another organism and depends on it for survival, often causing harm.
A medicine used to kill or stop the growth of bacteria.
A germ or microorganism that can cause disease.
The body's ability to resist or fight off a disease.
A powerful explosion that occurs at the end of a massive star's life.
